name: teamwork-task-test
description: Fetch a Teamwork.com task or whole tasklist by URL, extract acceptance criteria, and verify each criterion against the current repository — by running existing Pest / PHPUnit / Dusk / Cypress / Playwright / Vitest / Jest / Selenium tests where possible, by driving a real browser via the chrome-devtools MCP for visual checks, and by writing concrete manual scenarios for everything that cannot be automated. Beyond the stated criteria it always reviews four cross-cutting dimensions over the task's own diff — UI/UX and accessibility, performance, security, and page reachability (every registered screen must be reachable by clicking, not only by typing its URL) — plus an advisory fifth, framework best practices (recommendations only: the current idioms of the framework versions the project actually has installed; it never edits code and never fails a criterion), and proves every passing test is load-bearing with a negative control. Outputs a per-task report where each acceptance criterion is marked ✅ verified / ⚠️ partial / ❌ failed / 📋 manual / 📝 proposed, plus a separate findings table for the review dimensions and a short section of framework recommendations. Ticks met criteria to [x] in the Teamwork description under a byte-exact safety contract that preserves inline images; never moves the task or posts comments unless the user opts in. Shares the API token config with the `teamwork-task` plugin so setup is one-time. v1.3.0: work modes — `fast` means no test runs, no browser, no review dimensions and no negative control in one switch (deferred to `/work-mode full`); browser runners are never installed for a single run — a missing one is asked about once and then installed permanently. v1.4.0: the work modes follow the companion plugin's rename to `work-mode` 2.0.0 — `--mode=fast|full` (`full` by default), read from the project's `.claude/work-mode.local.md` whose global default is the `work-mode` plugin option `default_mode` in `/config`; the shared config's `mode` key is neither read nor written any more; the pre-rename flag values and mode file are still honoured for one version.
